solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Over time old British history can be interpreted as murderous

indicators.note: something that can be interpreted is open to being read another way, so these letters are to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as the word old
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grim reading of the national past: British history, looked at over time, turns out to be murderous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' is only a linking word here; the anagram, signalled by 'can be interpreted', works on T, OLD, B and HISTORY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone eager to kill or shed blood; they are close synonyms.

clue.text: Garrison placed ban on torture

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it, so the first word comes before the second

parts.note: to bar something is to ban it
the rack was an instrument of torture

explanation.surface: A military order: a garrison commander bans torture.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrack, usually in the plural, is a building where soldiers are housed, the home of a garrison; as a verb it also means to station troops.

clue.text: (Men may) regularly go for my power and hot sex appeal!

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other letter of the phrase go for my

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power
H stands for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A cheeky boast: men are drawn to my power and red-hot sex appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'go for my' are O, O, M. The bracketed 'Men may' is just scene-setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is informal for attractive energy or allure, the quality that makes someone sexy.

clue.text: Greyish-brown grease spoiled garment

parts.note: dun is a dull greyish-brown colour, as in a dun horse

indicators.note: spoiled means messed up, so the letters of grease are jumbled

explanation.surface: Greasy marks have ruined a drab brown item of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungarees are overalls or trousers with a bib, a work garment.

clue.text: Watch us snare concealed dog-fish

indicators.note: concealed tells us the answer lies tucked away inside the run of words Watch us snare

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep an eye on some fishermen trapping a hidden dogfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Huss is a fishmonger's name for dogfish, a small shark sold as food in Britain.

clue.text: What could secure two birds separated by one foot

indicators.note: the two birds are kept apart by something put between them

parts.note: the ree is the female ruff, a wading bird
the knot is a wading bird of the sandpiper family
F is the abbreviation for foot

explanation.surface: A puzzle about two birds kept a single foot apart.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole idea of something that could make fast, a usage typical of cryptic clues.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef knot is a secure, symmetrical knot used to tie two rope ends together, so it fastens things.

clue.text: Dry hemp fibres over end of fence line

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over what follows, so it comes first

parts.note: tow is the coarse broken fibre of hemp or flax

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Rough hemp fibres dry out, hung over the end of a fence line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' is a verb here, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To dry yourself after a bath you rub with this cloth; it is used as a verb meaning to wipe dry.

clue.text: After swallowing a lick of ice-cream silly ostrich becomes famous

indicators.note: swallowing means one piece takes another inside it
silly suggests the ostrich is behaving foolishly, so its letters are scrambled
a lick is just a small taste, so only the first letter is used

explanation.surface: A daft ostrich gulps a lick of ice cream and becomes a celebrity.
explanation.definitionFit: Historic means notable or important in history, so well known and celebrated.

clue.text: Tight police trap set by Yard

parts.note: a sting is an undercover police operation to trap criminals

explanation.surface: A tight police trap is set by Scotland Yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yard' suggests Scotland Yard, the London police headquarters, but it is the unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight in the sense of mean with money, unwilling to spend: a miserly synonym.

clue.text: Injured miner is caught close to incoherence in talk of the past

indicators.note: injured implies damaged, so the letters of miner is are rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A hurt miner, trapped, mumbles incoherently about old times.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to chat or think fondly about earlier days and memories.

clue.text: Become silent in game

definitions.meaning: an old word for being hushed or keeping quiet
a card game for four players in two partnerships

explanation.surface: Keep quiet during the game.
explanation.definitionFit: The card game is said to be named from the call for silence, an archaic sense meaning hush.

clue.text: Tree god's made of stone

parts.note: the ash is a common tree
a Lar is a Roman household god, one of the Lares

explanation.surface: A tree god's statue is carved from stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashlar is squared, dressed masonry; used attributively it describes walls built of cut blocks.

clue.text: A lot of seaweed found in crumbling stone framework

indicators.note: one piece is found inside the other
crumbling suggests breaking up, so the letters of stone are rearranged
a lot but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: kelp is a large brown seaweed

explanation.surface: A beachcomber finds heaps of seaweed lodged in crumbling rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Framework' is the definition; the seaweed and stone picture a beach, not a body.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton is the bony frame of an animal, and figuratively any basic supporting structure.

clue.text: Organ tuned in key D

indicators.note: tuning adjusts something into a new arrangement, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A church organ has been tuned in the key of D.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' looks musical alongside 'tuned' and 'key', but it is a body organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The kidney is one of the paired organs of the body that filter blood.

clue.text: Det. Force working to expose traitor

indicators.note: working means being worked on and reshaped, so the letters of Det Force are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A detective force is busy exposing a mole within its ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: A defector abandons their own side for the enemy, which is the conduct of a turncoat.

clue.text: Order ready without one once

parts.note: form can mean order or arrangement, as in good form

indicators.note: without signals that a piece is taken away

parts.note: early in the sense of prompt or ahead of time
a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: An order is ready, minus one item.
explanation.definitionFit: Once in the sense of at one time in the past, a direct synonym for previously.

clue.text: In lake catch up with last of eider duck

indicators.note: In places the catch inside the lake

parts.note: a mere is a lake or pond

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: a snag is a catch or hidden drawback

indicators.note: the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: On a lake a duck catches up with the trailing eider.
explanation.walkthrough: GANS (SNAG reversed by 'up') goes into MERE to give MERGANSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The merganser is a fish-eating diving bird with a saw-toothed bill, a species of the waterfowl family.

clue.text: Plan to study summit

parts.note: to con is an old word meaning to study or learn
a spire is a pointed top, a peak

explanation.surface: Planning to study at the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: To conspire is to plot together secretly, a scheming sense of plan.

clue.text: Tea is no fun mixed with a touch of ice

indicators.note: a touch is a small amount, so just the first letter
mixed shows the letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: Iced tea is no fun with only a touch of ice.
explanation.definitionFit: An infusion is a drink made by steeping leaves in hot water, which is how tea is brewed.

clue.text: Babe's popular number in Grease

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: fat is grease, as in cooking fat

explanation.surface: A babe's favourite number in the musical Grease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grease' suggests the musical with its popular numbers, but it simply means fat.
explanation.definitionFit: A babe is a baby, a very young child, which is what an infant is.

clue.text: Badgers brother about going to Kansas

parts.note: c, for circa, means about
KS is the postal abbreviation for Kansas

explanation.surface: Pestering a brother who is heading to Kansas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badgers' reads as a verb, to pester, but it is the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Brock is an old country name for the badger, used in folklore and children's stories.

clue.text: Has beer befuddled this creature?

indicators.note: befuddled means muddled with drink, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Has the beer made this animal tipsy?
explanation.definitionFit: The definition points to a female bear, a wild animal, which is what the hyphenated word names.

clue.text: Female's superb disguise? Hopefully with this!

parts.note: ace means excellent, superb
a mask is a disguise

explanation.surface: A woman's superb disguise, one she hopes will work.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the cryptic tail: the disguise works, one hopes, with the help of this covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A face mask covers the features and so hides identity, a protective or concealing cover.

clue.text: Greek character's thus in art

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quoted error

explanation.surface: A Greek figure appears thus in a work of art.
explanation.definitionFit: Music is one of the arts, as in the fine arts of painting, poetry and composition.

clue.text: Manipulate wife's opinion

parts.note: an angle is a point of view or opinion

explanation.surface: A wife's point of view manipulated.
explanation.definitionFit: To wangle is to get something by craft or trickery, a cunning form of manipulation.

clue.text: The Italian is involved in basic sin

indicators.note: is involved in places the first piece inside the second

parts.note: gut means instinctive or basic, as in a gut reaction
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: An Italian is mixed up in fundamental wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: Guilt is the state of having done wrong, culpability for an offence or transgression.

clue.text: Favourable slant of Socialist policies inspired nation first of all

indicators.note: first of all takes the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A political story: socialist policies first won over the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Spin is the presentation of news in a flattering light, the craft of the political press officer.

clue.text: Corners king trapped by endless snare

indicators.note: trapped by puts one piece inside the other
endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a noose is a snare or loop
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king is cornered in a trap with no way out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corners' reads as a verb but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Nooks are small recesses or secluded spots, sheltered corners of a room.

clue.text: Imperturbable four stuck in deadlock

indicators.note: stuck in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: an impasse is a deadlock or stalemate
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four people stuck in a stalemate who remain unruffled.
explanation.definitionFit: Impassive means showing no emotion, calm and unmoved, the same sense as hard to disturb.

clue.text: During filming entire crew's performance relies initially on him

indicators.note: a performance is a staging, a reworking, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
crew's taken with its s as part of the letters

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: On a film set, the whole crew's work depends on the person who wrote the script.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'crew's' supplies an S for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The man on whom a film relies is the person who writes the script, so the pronoun points to that author.
